input: Outline a children's book I want to illustrate

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Children's books vary enormously in length and structure — a 8-page picture book needs a very different outline than a 48-page chapter book, which changes how many scenes, beats, and spreads to plan.
The target age group defines vocabulary, sentence complexity, concept depth, and how much the illustrations carry the story versus the text.
Knowing whether the story idea already exists (a character, a theme, a premise) or is starting from scratch determines where the outline process begins.
Tone and genre — silly and humorous, gentle and soothing, adventurous, educational — shapes the narrative arc, pacing, and what the outline emphasises.
Whether this is for personal use, a self-publishing project, or a traditional publisher submission changes the format requirements and how polished the outline needs to be.
Understanding what the outline will be used for — a writing roadmap, a pitch document, a page-by-page illustration plan — determines the level of detail and structure needed.
Knowing the illustration style the user has in mind (full-bleed spreads, spot illustrations, black-and-white, etc.) affects how the outline maps text to visual moments on the page.

gold.taskTitle: Outline a children's book to illustrate
gold.taskDescription: Create a structured outline for an original children's book that the user plans to illustrate themselves.

questions.title: What age group is this book written for?
questions.description: Identify the target reader age — e.g., toddlers (0-3), picture book age (4-8), or early reader (6-10) — to set vocabulary, sentence length, and concept complexity.

questions.title: How long should the finished book be?
questions.description: Determine the intended page or word count — e.g., a 32-page picture book, a short 500-word story, or a longer early-reader format — to shape the outline's structure.

questions.title: Do you already have a story idea or starting premise?
questions.description: Find out whether the user has a character, conflict, theme, or rough plot in mind, or needs the outline to help generate the concept from scratch.

questions.title: What tone or genre fits your vision best?
questions.description: Clarify the overall feel — humorous and silly, warm and soothing, adventurous, educational, magical — to shape the narrative arc and pacing of the outline.

questions.title: Is this for personal use, self-publishing, or a publisher pitch?
questions.description: Determine the intended destination of the book to calibrate how formal, detailed, or submission-ready the outline needs to be.

questions.title: Will the outline serve as a writing guide or an illustration page plan?
questions.description: Understand the primary purpose of the outline — a narrative roadmap for writing the text, a spread-by-spread visual breakdown, or both — to set the right level of detail.

questions.title: What illustration style are you planning to use?
questions.description: Learn whether the user envisions full-bleed spreads, spot art with text blocks, black-and-white, or a particular medium, so the outline can map story beats to visual moments accordingly.
